name: Crispy Ragi Dosa
description: Nutrient-dense fermented crepes made with finger millet and black gram, naturally packed with calcium and iron.
instructions: Wash and soak ragi, black gram (urad dal), and raw rice together in water for 4-6 hours.
Grind the soaked grains in a wet grinder or high-speed blender into a smooth, pourable batter.
Add salt and allow the batter to naturally ferment in a warm spot for 8-10 hours.
Heat a seasoned cast-iron skillet, pour a ladle of batter, and spread thinly in concentric circles.
Drizzle virgin coconut oil along the edges and cook on medium flame until golden and crispy. Flip briefly and serve.

name: Kerala Cheera Thoran (Amaranth Coconut Stir-fry)
description: Traditional Kerala red amaranth greens sautéed with freshly grated coconut, shallots, and virgin coconut oil.
instructions: Wash red amaranth (cheera) leaves thoroughly under running water, drain, and finely chop.
Coarsely crush fresh coconut, shallots, green chillies, garlic, and turmeric powder in a mortar or spice blender.
Heat coconut oil in a pan, splutter mustard seeds, and add fresh curry leaves.
Add chopped cheera leaves and salt. Cover and cook on low heat for 5 minutes without adding extra water.
Stir in the coconut mixture, cook uncovered for 3-4 minutes until aromatic, and serve hot with steamed rice.

name: Traditional Kerala Avial
description: Wholesome melange of ash gourd, drumsticks, carrots, and beans gently cooked in a rustic coconut-curd sauce with curry leaves.
instructions: Cut ash gourd, carrots, and drumsticks into uniform 2-inch batons.
Simmer the vegetables with turmeric powder, green chillies, salt, and half a cup of water until fork-tender.
Grind freshly grated coconut and cumin seeds into a coarse paste without adding too much water.
Add the coconut paste to the cooked vegetables and let simmer gently for 2 minutes.
Turn off heat, stir in whisked fresh curd, top with a handful of fresh curry leaves, and drizzle raw coconut oil.

name: Malabar Kadala Curry (Black Chickpeas in Roasted Coconut)
description: Protein-dense whole black chickpeas simmered in a roasted coconut and fragrant spice reduction.
instructions: Soak black chickpeas (kala chana / kadala) overnight and pressure cook with salt until soft.
In a pan, dry-roast grated coconut, coriander seeds, and curry leaves until deep golden brown and aromatic.
Cool the roasted coconut mixture and grind into a rich, smooth paste.
Heat coconut oil, sauté sliced onions, ginger, garlic, and chopped tomatoes until softened.
Add the cooked chickpeas with their cooking broth and the coconut paste. Simmer for 10-12 minutes until gravy thickens.

name: Kerala Mild Vegetable Stew
description: Gentle coconut milk stew loaded with carrots, potatoes, and whole spices, perfect for easy digestion.
instructions: Extract fresh thin and thick coconut milk from grated coconut using warm water.
Sauté thinly sliced onions, ginger, green chillies, and curry leaves in coconut oil until translucent.
Add diced potatoes, carrots, and thin coconut milk with a pinch of salt. Simmer until vegetables are cooked.
Crush black pepper coarsely and stir in.
Pour in the thick coconut milk, heat on low flame without boiling, turn off heat, and serve with appam or rice.

name: Kerala Moru Kachiyathu (Seasoned Buttermilk Curry)
description: Probiotic-rich tempered buttermilk curry infused with ginger, garlic, turmeric, shallots, and curry leaves.
instructions: Whisk fresh curd with salt, turmeric powder, and 100ml water until smooth and lump-free.
Heat coconut oil in a clay pot or pan; splutter mustard seeds and cumin seeds.
Add thinly sliced shallots, crushed ginger, garlic, slit green chillies, and curry leaves. Sauté until fragrant.
Lower heat to minimum and pour in the whisked seasoned curd while stirring continuously.
Warm gently on low heat until steam starts rising (do not boil, to prevent curdling). Serve with warm rice.

name: Traditional Tamil Nadu Drumstick Sambar
description: Classic protein-packed toor dal stew simmered with drumsticks, shallots, ripe tomatoes, and fragrant sambar spices.
instructions: Pressure cook toor dal (red gram dal) with turmeric powder and water until soft and mushy; whisk smooth.
In a pot, extract tamarind juice in 1 cup of warm water; add drumstick pieces, shallots, tomatoes, and salt.
Boil until raw tamarind smell dissipates and drumsticks are tender.
Add the cooked toor dal and freshly pounded coriander-cumin sambar powder; simmer for 5 minutes.
Temper mustard seeds and curry leaves in hot gingelly (sesame) oil and pour into the bubbling sambar.

name: Pepper Tomato Rasam
description: Tangy and revitalizing South Indian broth infused with crushed black pepper, cumin, garlic, and ripe tomatoes.
instructions: Crush tomatoes by hand with tamarind extract, turmeric powder, and 300ml water.
In a mortar, coarsely crush black peppercorns, cumin seeds, and unpeeled garlic cloves.
Bring the tomato-tamarind broth to a boil until the raw aroma softens.
Add the crushed pepper-cumin-garlic mixture and bring to a gentle simmer until frothy (do not rolling boil).
Temper mustard seeds and curry leaves in ghee, pour over rasam, and garnish generously with fresh coriander leaves.

name: Classic Tamil Ven Pongal
description: Comforting porridge of raw rice and yellow moong dal tempered with golden cashews, cumin, ginger, and desi ghee.
instructions: Lightly roast yellow moong dal in a dry pan until aromatic, then mix with washed raw rice.
Pressure cook the rice and dal mixture with 4 cups of water and salt until very soft and creamy.
Heat ghee in a small pan; add whole black peppercorns, cumin seeds, and finely chopped ginger.
Add fresh curry leaves and sauté until the cumin is fragrant.
Pour the sizzling ghee tempering directly into the cooked pongal and mix thoroughly until velvety.

name: Keerai Moong Kootu (Spinach Lentil Stew)
description: Nourishing and mildly spiced Tamil stew combining fresh spinach, yellow moong dal, and a cumin-coconut paste.
instructions: Pressure cook moong dal with turmeric powder and water until soft.
Wash and chop spinach; add to cooked dal with half a cup of water and cook for 5 minutes.
Grind coconut, green chillies, and cumin seeds into a fine paste.
Add the coconut paste and salt to the simmering spinach-dal mixture; cook for 3 minutes.
Temper mustard seeds in coconut oil, stir into kootu, and serve warm.

name: Temple Sundal (Spiced Tempered Chickpeas)
description: Protein-rich white chickpeas tossed with mustard seeds, curry leaves, ginger, and fresh grated coconut.
instructions: Soak chickpeas or chana dal in water for 2-4 hours, then boil with salt until cooked yet firm.
Heat gingelly oil in a pan, add mustard seeds and let them crackle.
Add slit green chillies, finely grated ginger, and curry leaves; sauté for 30 seconds.
Add the drained cooked chickpeas and toss over medium heat for 2 minutes to absorb seasonings.
Turn off heat, fold in freshly grated coconut, and serve as an energy-dense tea-time snack.

name: Paruppu Urundai Rasam (Lentil Dumpling Broth)
description: Steamed spiced toor and chana dal dumplings bathed in a soothing, tangy rasam broth.
instructions: Soak toor and chana dal together for 1 hour; grind coarsely with salt and cumin seeds into a thick paste.
Shape the lentil paste into small lime-sized balls and steam in an idli steamer for 8-10 minutes.
Simmer tamarind extract with chopped tomatoes, turmeric powder, and salt until raw flavor dissipates.
Add crushed black pepper, cumin, and garlic to the simmering rasam broth.
Gently drop the steamed lentil dumplings into the rasam, simmer for 2 minutes, and serve hot.

name: Drumstick Leaves (Moringa) Poriyal
description: Iron and calcium powerhouse: fresh drumstick leaves sautéed with shallots, crushed cumin, and fresh coconut.
instructions: Strip drumstick leaves (moringa keerai) from stalks, wash thoroughly, and drain well.
Heat gingelly oil in a skillet, splutter mustard seeds, and sauté sliced shallots with green chillies until soft.
Add the drumstick leaves and salt; sauté on medium heat without covering until wilted (approx 5 minutes).
Ensure the moisture evaporates completely and the greens are tender.
Toss in fresh grated coconut, stir for 1 minute, and remove from heat.

name: Karnataka Bisi Bele Bath
description: Iconic Karnataka one-pot meal of rice and toor dal simmered with vegetables and freshly ground aromatic spices.
instructions: Cook rice and toor dal together in a pressure cooker with 4.5 cups of water until very soft.
Boil carrots, drumsticks, and shallots in tamarind water with salt until tender.
Roast coriander seeds, cumin, and red chillies; grind into fragrant Bisi Bele Bath powder.
Combine cooked dal-rice, cooked vegetables, and spice powder; simmer on low heat for 8 minutes.
Temper mustard seeds and curry leaves in ghee, pour into bath, and serve steaming hot.

name: Ragi Mudde with Bassaru
description: Traditional rustic Karnataka finger millet dumplings served with a nutrient-dense spiced lentil broth.
instructions: Boil toor dal and spinach in water until cooked; strain the nutritious broth (saaru water) into a bowl.
In a heavy pot, boil 240ml water with a tsp of ghee; slowly sprinkle ragi flour while stirring vigorously to avoid lumps.
Cover and steam ragi dough on low heat for 5 minutes; shape into smooth spherical balls (mudde) using wet hands.
For the bassaru, grind a small portion of cooked dal with garlic, cumin, pepper, and tomatoes; stir into the broth.
Simmer the saaru for 5 minutes and serve alongside the warm ragi mudde with a dab of ghee.

name: Karnataka Akki Roti
description: Crisp and flavorful rice flour flatbreads studded with finely chopped onions, fresh coriander, cumin, and green chillies.
instructions: In a wide bowl, mix fine rice flour, finely diced onions, coriander leaves, chopped green chillies, cumin, and grated coconut.
Add warm water gradually to knead into a soft, pliable dough.
Pat a ball of dough thinly directly onto a greased pan or banana leaf using wet fingertips.
Make small steam holes in the roti, drizzle coconut oil, and cook covered on medium heat until base turns golden and crisp.
Flip and cook the other side for 1 minute; serve hot with coconut chutney or spiced dal.

name: Hesarubele Kosambari (Moong Cucumber Salad)
description: Light and refreshing Karnataka salad made with soaked yellow moong dal, crunchy cucumbers, grated coconut, and lemon.
instructions: Soak yellow moong dal in water for 45 minutes; drain completely.
Finely dice the fresh cucumber and mix with drained moong dal, grated coconut, and chopped coriander.
Temper mustard seeds and finely minced green chillies in hot coconut oil.
Pour the tempering over the salad.
Squeeze fresh lemon juice, add salt just before serving, and toss well.

name: Menthya Soppu Pulao (Fenugreek Leaf Rice)
description: Fragrant Karnataka style rice pilaf packed with bitter-sweet fresh fenugreek leaves, peas, and whole spices.
instructions: Wash and pluck tender fresh methi (fenugreek) leaves; chop finely.
Heat ghee in a pot, add cumin seeds, sliced onions, minced ginger, and garlic; sauté until golden.
Add chopped fenugreek leaves and turmeric powder; sauté for 3-4 minutes to mellow the bitterness.
Stir in washed raw rice and sauté for 1 minute.
Add 2.5 cups of water and salt; cover and cook on low heat for 15 minutes until grains are fluffy.

name: Karnataka Majjige Huli (Ash Gourd Buttermilk Stew)
description: Succulent ash gourd simmered in a spiced coconut-curd gravy flavored with cumin, ginger, and mustard.
instructions: Dice ash gourd into cubes and boil with turmeric powder and salt until translucent and tender.
Grind fresh grated coconut, green chillies, ginger, and cumin seeds into a smooth paste.
Add the coconut paste to the cooked ash gourd and simmer for 3 minutes.
Turn off heat and stir in whisked yogurt (curd) smoothly.
Temper mustard seeds and curry leaves in hot coconut oil and pour over the gravy.

name: Andhra Tomato Pappu
description: Tangy and hearty Andhra style toor dal cooked with ripe tomatoes, green chillies, and a generous garlic-mustard tadka.
instructions: In a pressure cooker, combine toor dal, chopped tomatoes, green chillies, turmeric, and 2 cups of water.
Cook for 4 whistles until dal is thoroughly softened; mash coarsely with a wooden masher (dal thaduka) and add salt.
Heat ghee in a tadka pan; add mustard seeds, cumin seeds, and crushed garlic cloves.
Sauté until garlic turns fragrant and golden brown, then toss in fresh curry leaves.
Pour the sizzling garlic tadka directly into the mashed dal, mix well, and serve with hot rice and ghee.

name: Andhra Pesarattu (Whole Moong Dosa)
description: High-protein unfermented crepes made from soaked whole green moong beans, blended with fresh ginger and green chillies.
instructions: Soak whole green moong and raw rice in water for 4-6 hours; drain well.
Grind with ginger, green chillies, cumin seeds, and salt into a smooth, thick batter (no fermentation needed).
Heat a tawa on medium-high; pour a ladle of batter and spread into a thin round crepe.
Sprinkle finely diced onions on top, press lightly with a spatula, and drizzle peanut oil along the edges.
Cook until golden brown and crisp underneath. Fold and serve hot with ginger chutney.

name: Tangy Palak-Tamarind Andhra Dal
description: Spicy and tangy Andhra lentil preparation featuring fresh spinach cooked with tamarind, green chillies, and garlic.
instructions: Pressure cook toor dal with chopped spinach, slit green chillies, tamarind pulp, and turmeric until tender.
Mash the cooked dal and spinach thoroughly with a wooden ladle until creamy; add salt.
Heat ghee in a pan, add mustard seeds, and sauté crushed garlic cloves until golden brown.
Pour the hot tadka into the mashed spinach dal.
Simmer for 2 minutes to meld flavors and serve hot with steamed rice.

name: Andhra Majjiga Pulusu (Vegetable Buttermilk Stew)
description: Tangy Andhra yogurt stew loaded with bottle gourd or ash gourd, seasoned with ginger-green chilli paste and mustard.
instructions: Soak chana dal for 20 minutes; grind with ginger and green chillies into a smooth seasoning paste.
Boil ash gourd pieces in water with turmeric and salt until tender.
Whisk curd with 1 cup of water and the ground dal-ginger paste; pour into the cooked ash gourd.
Heat gently on low heat while stirring continuously until warm (do not boil).
Temper mustard seeds and curry leaves in oil, add to the stew, and turn off heat.

name: Andhra Masala Vada
description: Crunchy golden chana dal fritters packed with chopped onions, fresh ginger, mint, and fennel notes.
instructions: Soak chana dal in water for 2 hours; reserve 2 tablespoons of whole dal and drain the rest.
Coarsely grind the drained dal with cumin, green chillies, and ginger without adding water.
Mix in the reserved whole dal, finely diced onions, chopped curry leaves, and salt.
Shape small portions of dough into flat round patties.
Shallow-fry or bake in peanut oil on medium flame until deep golden and crunchy.

name: Andhra Bendakaya Vepudu (Crisp Okra Stir-fry)
description: Crispy sliced okra stir-fried with roasted peanuts, crushed garlic, and flavorful Andhra spices.
instructions: Wash okra (bendakaya) and dry completely with a clean towel; slice into 1/2-inch rounds.
Heat peanut oil in a wide pan; roast peanuts until golden, then set aside.
In the same oil, add mustard seeds, curry leaves, and crushed garlic cloves.
Add the sliced okra and turmeric; sauté uncovered on medium heat for 12 minutes until crisp and non-slimy.
Toss in the roasted peanuts and salt just before turning off heat.

name: Palak Moong Dal (Spinach Lentil Stew)
description: Nourishing yellow lentils simmered with fresh spinach, fragrant garlic, ginger, and turmeric.
instructions: Rinse yellow moong dal and cook with water, salt, and turmeric in a pressure cooker until soft.
Wash and finely chop fresh spinach leaves.
Heat ghee in a pan, sauté cumin, diced onions, ginger, garlic, and chopped tomatoes until oil releases.
Add chopped spinach and cook for 3-4 minutes until wilted.
Pour in the cooked moong dal, adjust consistency with water, and simmer for 5 minutes.

name: Fresh Methi Paratha
description: Whole wheat flatbreads kneaded with fresh fenugreek leaves and mild spices, cooked golden with desi ghee.
instructions: Pluck, wash, and finely chop fresh fenugreek (methi) leaves.
In a large bowl, mix whole wheat flour (atta), chopped methi, cumin, turmeric, salt, and a tsp of ghee.
Add warm water gradually and knead into a smooth, non-sticky dough. Rest for 10 minutes.
Divide into balls and roll out into thin round parathas.
Cook on a hot tawa with a dab of desi ghee on both sides until golden speckles appear.

name: Chole Palak (Chickpea & Spinach Curry)
description: Hearty chickpeas and fresh spinach simmered in a spiced onion-tomato reduction with garlic and ginger.
instructions: Soak chickpeas overnight and pressure cook with salt until completely soft.
Blanch spinach leaves in boiling water for 2 minutes, shock in cold water, and blend into a bright green purée.
Heat oil in a pan; sauté cumin, diced onions, ginger, and garlic until caramelized.
Add puréed tomatoes and spices; cook until oil separates.
Add the cooked chickpeas and spinach purée; simmer for 8-10 minutes to blend flavors.

name: Paneer & Crushed Pumpkin Seed Bhurji
description: Crumbled artisanal cottage cheese scrambled with roasted pumpkin seeds, diced onions, tomatoes, and haldi.
instructions: Crumble fresh paneer with your fingers; lightly dry roast pumpkin seeds until aromatic and coarsely crush.
Heat ghee in a pan, sauté diced onions and green chillies until soft and translucent.
Add chopped tomatoes, turmeric, and salt; cook until tomatoes turn soft.
Toss in the crumbled paneer and crushed pumpkin seeds; stir on medium heat for 2-3 minutes.
Garnish with chopped coriander and serve hot with rotis or whole grain toast.

name: Homestyle Yellow Dal Tadka
description: Classic comfort food: split pigeon peas (toor dal) cooked soft and finished with a sizzling cumin, garlic, and ghee tadka.
instructions: Pressure cook toor dal with turmeric, half the ginger, salt, and water for 4 whistles until completely tender.
Heat ghee in a pan; add cumin seeds and allow them to sizzle.
Add finely chopped garlic, remaining ginger, and onions; sauté until golden brown.
Add chopped tomatoes and cook until soft and pulpy.
Pour the cooked dal into the pan, simmer for 5 minutes, garnish with fresh coriander, and serve.

name: Homestyle Palak Paneer
description: Succulent cubes of cottage cheese simmered in a velvety purée of fresh spinach spiced with cumin, garlic, and ginger.
instructions: Blanch washed spinach in boiling salted water for 2 minutes, shock in ice water, and blend into a smooth puree.
Heat ghee in a skillet; add cumin seeds, chopped garlic, ginger, and onions. Sauté until lightly browned.
Add chopped tomatoes and salt; cook until soft.
Pour in the spinach puree and simmer on low heat for 5 minutes.
Gently fold in paneer cubes, cook for 2 minutes until paneer is soft, and serve warm with roti.

name: Slow-Simmered Punjabi Rajma
description: Tender red kidney beans simmered in a thick, spiced onion-tomato gravy infused with ginger, garlic, and whole spices.
instructions: Soak red kidney beans (rajma) overnight in water; pressure cook with salt for 20-25 minutes until melt-in-mouth tender.
Heat ghee in a heavy pot, add cumin seeds, finely diced onions, minced garlic, and ginger; sauté until caramelized.
Add tomato puree and turmeric; cook until oil releases from the sides.
Add the boiled rajma with its cooking liquid; mash a few spoonfuls against the pot to thicken the gravy.
Simmer on low heat for 15 minutes, allowing spices to penetrate the beans. Serve hot with steamed rice.

name: Comforting Moong Dal Khichdi
description: Soothing, easily digestible Ayurvedic staple of yellow moong lentils and rice simmered with ghee, cumin, and ginger.
instructions: Wash raw rice and yellow moong dal together; soak for 15 minutes.
Heat ghee in a pressure cooker; add cumin seeds, crushed black pepper, and minced ginger.
Add the drained rice, dal, turmeric powder, and salt; sauté gently for 1 minute.
Add 4.5 cups of water for a comforting, porridge-like consistency.
Pressure cook for 3-4 whistles; let pressure release naturally, mix with an extra spoon of warm ghee, and serve.

name: Homestyle Aloo Gobi Matar
description: Tender cauliflower florets, potatoes, and green peas sautéed with cumin, turmeric, ginger, and fresh coriander.
instructions: Cut cauliflower into florets and potatoes into small cubes.
Heat mustard oil in a pan until lightly smoking; add cumin seeds and minced ginger.
Add potato cubes, cauliflower florets, turmeric, and salt; stir well.
Cover and cook on low heat for 12 minutes, stirring occasionally until potatoes are fork tender.
Add chopped tomatoes, cook uncovered for 4 minutes until dry and fragrant, and garnish with fresh coriander.

name: Kanda Batata Poha
description: Flattened rice tempered with turmeric, crunchy roasted peanuts, mustard seeds, diced potatoes, and fresh lime.
instructions: Rinse thick poha (rice flakes) in a colander under running water for 30 seconds; drain and rest for 5 minutes.
Heat peanut oil in a pan; fry peanuts until crunchy and golden, then set aside.
In the same oil, splutter mustard seeds, curry leaves, green chillies, and finely diced potatoes. Cook until potatoes soften.
Add finely chopped onions and turmeric; sauté until onions turn translucent.
Gently fold in the softened poha, salt, and fried peanuts. Steam covered for 2 minutes; finish with fresh lemon juice.

name: Gujarati Methi Thepla
description: Soft spiced flatbreads made with whole wheat, gram flour, fresh fenugreek leaves, sesame seeds, and yogurt.
instructions: Finely chop washed fenugreek leaves; mix with whole wheat flour, besan (chana flour), white sesame seeds, and spices.
Add yogurt, 1 tsp oil, and warm water; knead into a very soft, pliable dough.
Roll into very thin round discs using dry flour dusting.
Cook on a hot tawa with a light brush of oil on both sides until soft golden spots appear.
Stack wrapped in a clean cloth to retain softness; perfect for travel and daily nourishment.

name: Gujarati Khatti Meethi Dal
description: Harmonious toor dal with a balance of sweet, spicy, and tangy flavors, simmered with peanuts, ginger, and mustard.
instructions: Pressure cook toor dal with peanuts, chopped tomatoes, turmeric, and 2.5 cups of water until soft; blend with hand whisk.
Stir in tamarind extract, grated ginger, and salt; bring to a simmer.
Heat ghee in a tadka ladle, splutter mustard seeds and cumin seeds.
Pour the tempering into the simmering dal.
Simmer gently for 8-10 minutes until aromatic and silky.

name: Maharashtrian Sprouted Moong Usal
description: Vibrant sprouted green moong stir-fried with mustard, curry leaves, onions, turmeric, and fresh coconut.
instructions: Steam sprouted whole green moong for 5 minutes so they remain slightly crisp.
Heat peanut oil in a kadai; splutter mustard seeds and curry leaves.
Add finely chopped onions, ginger, and garlic; sauté until translucent.
Add tomatoes, turmeric, and salt; cook until tomatoes break down.
Add the steamed sprouted moong, toss for 3 minutes, and garnish with freshly grated coconut.

name: Gujarati Sambhariya Bhindi
description: Tender okra slit and pan-roasted with a savory stuffing of roasted peanuts, sesame seeds, coriander, and turmeric.
instructions: Wipe dry and trim okra; make a lengthwise slit without cutting all the way through.
Coarsely grind roasted peanuts, sesame seeds, coriander seeds, turmeric, and salt to make the masala stuffing.
Stuff the prepared masala into the slit okra.
Heat peanut oil in a wide pan; place stuffed okra in a single layer.
Cook covered on low heat for 10-12 minutes, turning gently halfway until tender and crisp; finish with lemon juice.

name: Maharashtrian Koshimbir / Kachumber Salad
description: Crisp diced cucumbers and tomatoes dressed with crushed roasted peanuts, fresh coriander, green chilli, and lemon juice.
instructions: Finely dice fresh cucumbers, ripe tomatoes, and onions.
Coarsely crush roasted peanuts using a rolling pin or mortar.
In a salad bowl, toss together the vegetables, crushed peanuts, and finely chopped coriander.
Drizzle fresh lemon juice and season with a pinch of salt.
Toss immediately before serving to maintain maximum crunch.

name: Upwas Style Spiced Potato & Peanut Toss
description: Boiled potato cubes sautéed with roasted crushed peanuts, cumin seeds, green chillies, and lemon.
instructions: Boil potatoes until tender, peel, and cut into bite-sized cubes.
Coarsely crush roasted peanuts.
Heat ghee in a pan; add cumin seeds and finely chopped green chillies.
Add the potato cubes, crushed peanuts, and salt; stir-fry on medium flame for 5 minutes until lightly crispy.
Finish with fresh lemon juice and chopped coriander.

name: Bengali Chholar Dal with Coconut
description: Fragrant festive Bengal gram (chana dal) flavored with whole spices, ginger, and fried coconut flakes.
instructions: Soak chana dal for 1 hour; pressure cook with turmeric, salt, and water until cooked but holding its shape.
Cut coconut into tiny thin slices (kuchi); fry in ghee until golden brown and aromatic, then set aside.
In the same ghee, temper cumin seeds and freshly grated ginger paste.
Pour in the cooked dal with its liquid; simmer for 8 minutes to thicken slightly.
Fold in the fried coconut flakes and an extra drizzle of ghee before serving.

name: Crispy Bengali Begun Bhaja
description: Thick eggplant rounds marinated in turmeric, salt, and mild spices, shallow fried in pure mustard oil.
instructions: Slice eggplant into thick round discs (approx 3/4-inch).
Rub thoroughly with turmeric powder and salt; let rest for 5 minutes to release excess water.
Heat mustard oil in a heavy iron skillet until hot.
Place eggplant rounds in a single layer and shallow fry on medium heat.
Flip and cook until both sides are deeply golden and the flesh is tender and creamy.

name: Bengali Dimer Dalna (Homestyle Egg Curry)
description: Hard-boiled eggs and tender potato halves simmered in a light, warming ginger-tomato-garlic curry.
instructions: Boil eggs until hard, peel, and lightly prick with a fork; coat with turmeric and salt.
Shallow-fry the boiled eggs and halved potato cubes in hot mustard oil until golden; set aside.
In the remaining oil, temper cumin seeds and sauté sliced onions, ginger, and garlic paste.
Add chopped tomatoes, turmeric, and salt; cook down into a rich masala paste.
Add 1.5 cups water, the fried eggs, and potatoes. Simmer covered for 10 minutes until potatoes are soft.

name: Simple Bengali Masoor Dal
description: Light and comforting red lentil soup gently tempered with cumin, green chillies, and fresh coriander.
instructions: Wash red masoor dal and boil with water, turmeric, and slit green chillies until soft.
Whisk the dal into a smooth, light soup consistency.
Heat mustard oil in a tadka pan; add cumin seeds and sliced onions. Sauté until onions are golden.
Pour the tadka into the bubbling dal.
Simmer for 2 minutes, finish with fresh coriander leaves, and serve with steamed rice.

name: Bengali Aloo Til Posto Style
description: Tender potato cubes simmered in a fragrant white sesame and green chilli paste cooked in pungent mustard oil.
instructions: Soak white sesame seeds (til) in warm water for 15 minutes; grind with green chillies and salt into a smooth thick paste.
Dice potatoes into cubes.
Heat mustard oil in a kadai, add potato cubes and turmeric; sauté for 3-4 minutes.
Add half a cup of water, cover, and cook on low flame until potatoes are fork tender.
Stir in the sesame paste and 1 tsp raw mustard oil. Cook for 2 minutes and remove from heat.

name: Bengali Shorshe Machh (Mustard Fish Curry)
description: Tender freshwater fish simmered in an invigorating mustard and green chilli emulsion with virgin mustard oil.
instructions: Soak mustard seeds in warm water with a pinch of salt; grind with green chillies into a smooth paste.
Marinate cleaned fish with turmeric and salt; lightly sear in hot mustard oil for 1 minute per side.
Strain the mustard paste with 1 cup of water into the pan.
Bring to a gentle simmer on low heat; add slit green chillies and salt.
Simmer for 6-8 minutes until fish is cooked through; finish with a drizzle of raw mustard oil.

name: Overnight Chia & Berry Oats
description: Rolled oats and chia seeds soaked in protein-rich yogurt, topped with soaked almonds.
instructions: In a clean glass jar, combine rolled oats, chia seeds, and fresh whisked yogurt.
Add 50ml water or milk to adjust consistency and stir thoroughly.
Seal the jar and refrigerate overnight (or at least 4 hours) for chia and oats to soften.
Roughly chop soaked almonds.
Top the soaked oats with almonds and enjoy cold.

name: Mediterranean Quinoa & Pumpkin Seed Bowl
description: Nutty quinoa tossed with baby spinach, sweet cherry tomatoes, red onions, and crunchy pepitas.
instructions: Rinse quinoa under cold running water; cook in 200ml boiling water with salt for 15 minutes until fluffy.
Let quinoa cool to room temperature.
Dice tomatoes and thinly slice red onions; wash baby spinach.
In a salad bowl, toss cooked quinoa with spinach, tomatoes, and onions.
Dress with fresh lemon juice and top with crunchy toasted pumpkin seeds.

name: Pan-Seared Wild Salmon on Sautéed Greens
description: Tender wild salmon seared golden in garlic-infused oil over tender wilted spinach and ginger.
instructions: Pat wild salmon fillets dry with paper towels; season with salt and fresh black pepper.
Heat a skillet on medium-high; sear salmon skin-side down for 4-5 minutes until crisp.
Flip and sear the other side for 3-4 minutes until cooked through; remove from pan.
In the same skillet, add minced garlic, ginger, and washed spinach; sauté for 2 minutes until wilted.
Plate the sautéed spinach, rest the salmon fillet on top, and squeeze fresh lemon juice.

name: Spiced Sweet Potato & Beetroot Hash
description: Steamed cubes of sweet potato and beetroot pan-tossed with ginger, turmeric, and fresh lemon juice.
instructions: Peel sweet potato and beetroot; cut into uniform 1/2-inch cubes.
Steam cubes for 8-10 minutes until tender but firm.
Heat coconut oil in a pan, add minced ginger, and sauté for 1 minute.
Add the steamed root vegetables and toss on medium-high heat until slightly caramelized.
Season with salt, remove from heat, and drizzle with fresh lemon juice.

name: Mediterranean Shakshuka (Poached Eggs in Tomato Pepper Sauce)
description: Eggs gently poached in a simmering, smoky reduction of ripe tomatoes, sweet bell peppers, onions, garlic, and cumin.
instructions: Heat oil in a heavy skillet; sauté cumin seeds, diced onions, bell peppers, and minced garlic until softened.
Add chopped tomatoes, paprika, and salt; simmer on medium heat for 10 minutes until sauce is thick and saucy.
Use a spoon to create small wells in the tomato sauce.
Crack the fresh eggs directly into the wells.
Cover the skillet and simmer on low heat for 5-7 minutes until egg whites are set but yolks remain runny; garnish with coriander.

name: Mediterranean Chickpea & Cucumber Salad
description: Crisp cucumbers, juicy tomatoes, and hearty chickpeas tossed with fresh lemon juice and aromatic herbs.
instructions: Use pre-boiled or sprouted chickpeas (kala chana or kabuli chana); drain well.
Dice cucumbers, tomatoes, and red onions into uniform small cubes.
In a salad bowl, toss the chickpeas with the diced vegetables.
Dress with freshly squeezed lemon juice, salt, and black pepper.
Garnish with chopped fresh coriander or parsley and serve chilled.

name: Mediterranean Lemon Lentil & Spinach Soup
description: Hearty whole brown lentils simmered with baby spinach, tomatoes, garlic, and finished with a bright splash of fresh lemon.
instructions: Heat oil in a soup pot; sauté cumin, diced onions, and minced garlic until aromatic.
Add rinsed lentils, chopped tomatoes, salt, and 3.5 cups of water.
Simmer covered for 20 minutes until lentils are soft and tender.
Stir in the chopped fresh spinach and simmer for an additional 3 minutes.
Turn off heat, stir in fresh lemon juice, adjust seasoning, and serve with crusty bread.

name: Protein-Packed Egg & Baby Spinach Morning Scramble
description: Soft-scrambled farm fresh eggs folded with sautéed tender spinach, sweet tomatoes, and a crack of black pepper.
instructions: Whisk eggs with salt and freshly cracked black pepper in a small bowl.
Heat ghee in a non-stick skillet; sauté diced onions and tomatoes for 2 minutes.
Add chopped spinach leaves and sauté until wilted (approx 1 minute).
Lower heat to medium-low, pour in the whisked eggs, and gently sweep across the pan with a spatula.
Remove from heat while eggs are still soft and creamy. Serve immediately.
